[USER] User requested a checklist of InDesign cover tasks that need to be completed before ordering a print run.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided a checklist of InDesign cover tasks, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Check the document size: Ensure that the document size is the correct size for your final printed piece.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Bleed: Make sure that your artwork extends beyond the trim area by at least 1/8 inch on all sides to ensure that there is no white border around your final printed piece.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Crop marks: Add crop marks to the document to indicate where the paper should be trimmed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Color mode: Ensure that the document is in CMYK mode to ensure accurate color representation in print.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Resolution: Ensure that all images are at least 300 dpi to ensure that they print at a high quality.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Fonts: Embed all fonts in the document to ensure that they are available for the print run.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Layers: Flatten all layers in the document to ensure that there are no issues with transparency or overlapping elements.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Proofread: Double-check all text and graphics for errors and ensure that they are aligned properly.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. Export: Export the document as a print-ready PDF, making sure to choose the correct settings for your printer.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Check final PDF: Double-check the final PDF for any errors or issues before sending it off to the printer.
